item.title: listItems follows next_cursor
item.brief: Change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, sending no cursor on the first request and passing the cursor back unchanged. Update the README to document this. Keep npm test passing and add tests for multi-page, single-page, and absent-next_cursor cases. Commit in this repository only; do not push or merge.

pr.body:
Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no query on the first request and {cursor} afterwards, stopping when next_cursor is null or absent. A Set of seen cursors makes a server that repeats a cursor fail instead of looping forever. A page body that is not an object with an items array throws a descriptive error.

Files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md.

Checks: npm test -> 10 tests, 10 pass, 0 fail (multi-page, single-page, absent next_cursor, null/non-object body, repeated cursor, failing later page).

Review: three whole-change reviews on ba8647c and one delta review on 99110bb, all pass. Their findings (repeated cursor, null body) were fixed in 99110bb.

Open follow-up (non-blocking): the repeated-cursor Set compares object cursors by reference, so a non-string next_cursor repeating by value is not detected. The API uses string cursors. Rejecting non-string cursors would close this.

Assumptions: next_cursor is a string or null/absent, per the shared contract.
pr.summary: listItems follows next_cursor across pages. Before: returned only the first page of GET /items. Now: returns every item in order; first request has no cursor, later requests pass the cursor back unchanged. Repeated cursors and malformed pages throw.
pr.title: feat: make listItems follow next_cursor across pages

agt_01M8ARQQTVRXYXPE5SPRC2A4QQ:1.description: The do/while loop has no guard against a server that keeps returning the same next_cursor, so listItems would loop forever and keep growing items. at client.js:18 (remedy: Track seen cursors in a Set and throw a descriptive error on a repeat, or cap the page count, then add a test for a repeated cursor.)

agt_01M8ARQX3GVWQKF5MD9E0Y21WJ:1.description: listItems loops until next_cursor is null or absent, with no check for a cursor that repeats or a page limit. at client.js:18 (remedy: Track the cursors already sent in a Set and throw a descriptive error when one repeats, or cap the number of pages. Add a test where the server always returns the same cursor.)

agt_01M8ARQX3GVWQKF5MD9E0Y21WJ:2.description: If the response body is null or not an object, `body.items` throws a bare TypeError before the intended 'without an items array' message is reached. at client.js:21 (remedy: Check `body !== null && typeof body === 'object'` before reading `body.items`, or wrap the access in one guard that throws the same descriptive error.)

agt_01M8ARR26R11EYHD3VEJ5BKNZQ:1.description: The do/while loop has no guard against a server that returns the same next_cursor repeatedly. It would request forever and keep growing `items`. at client.js:21 (remedy: Track seen cursors in a Set and throw a descriptive error when a cursor repeats, or cap the page count.)

agt_01M8ARS62CSBG9CS8YZF9MWTNF:1.description: Repeated-cursor guard uses a Set, which compares object cursors by reference, so a non-string next_cursor that repeats by value (e.g. {p:1} twice) is not detected and the loop continues. at client.js:27 (remedy: Optionally reject non-string cursors at the boundary (throw if cursor is present and typeof cursor !== 'string') or compare JSON.stringify(cursor) in the Set.)

risk.why: client.js: listItems behaviour changes from one request to a paging loop, contained behind the existing transport interface. Tests cover the new paths. No security, persistence or API surface changes. Reviewers agreed on medium.

item.title: Cursor pagination for GET /items
item.brief: Add cursor pagination to GET /items as described in the shared contract: optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor query parameters; body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items ordered by id; 400 with {"error": "..."} for an invalid limit or cursor. Update the README to document the new parameters and response. Keep python3 -m unittest passing and add tests for paging, limits, and 400 cases. Commit in this repository only; do not push or merge.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

pr.body: Approach: cursor is the last returned id as a decimal string; a page holds ids greater than the cursor, sorted by id, with next_cursor set when more items remain. Digit strings are capped at 18 characters before int() so oversized input returns 400 instead of raising. Files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest on 4948b57 gives 10 tests OK. Review: three whole-change reviewers (agt_01M8ARR6Y91ZJX9S487KE633QD, agt_01M8ARRCPEPC7HVRNS9FZ1QRDY, agt_01M8ARRJFA11C969E9Z7HS1KH5) read base 0e761c5 through 9ca9cd2 and failed on the oversized-digit crash and a decorative assert; fixed in 4948b57 with Review-Fix trailers. Delta reviewer agt_01M8ART7Z98XWHJ8J3S1BPW7HF read 9ca9cd2..4948b57 and passed head 4948b57 with all six findings resolved. Open follow-up (non-blocking): get_item (GET /items/<id>) still uses str.isdigit and int() without the length cap, so a very long or superscript-digit id can raise; outside this change. Assumptions: cursor is id-based but documented as opaque; inventory-client adoption is a sibling item, not in this change.

risk.why: Contained feature behind the existing handle() interface, changing GET /items with an additive next_cursor key and new 400 paths. Touches api.py, test_api.py, README.md; behaviour changes plus tests. Three reviewers found the oversized-input crash, fixed and re-verified by a delta reviewer.
